examples.name: Grid
examples.code:
<Grid
  rows={['xxsmall', 'xsmall']}
  columns={['xsmall', 'small']}
  gap="small"
  areas={[
    { name: 'header', start: [0, 0], end: [1, 0] },
    { name: 'nav', start: [0, 1], end: [0, 1] },
    { name: 'main', start: [1, 1], end: [1, 1] },
  ]}
>
  <Box gridArea="header" background="brand" />
  <Box gridArea="nav" background="light-5" />
  <Box gridArea="main" background="light-2" />
</Grid>

prose.title: React/DOM Properties
prose.text:
At its core, the Grid component is a regular <div> element. Thus, both DOM and React properties, methods, and events are accessible. To read up on all of the possible DOM attributes and types available for div elements, check out this [MDN Web Documents page.](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/div) To learn more about DOM events and methods, you can read more on the [MDN Web Events documentation page](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Events).

Also, feel free to read about the [types of React events available](https://reactjs.org/docs/handling-events.html), or see [how DOM attributes change in React.](https://reactjs.org/docs/dom-elements.html) Working in tandem with Styled Components, you also have access to the [as property.](https://styled-components.com/docs/api#as-polymorphic-prop)
